Thanks for reaching out. A few clarifications before we lock a time: we mainly need read-only access for code scanning and commit metadata, but we do plan to set status checks (so write access for statuses only would be useful).

We mostly use GitHub Cloud for most repos but have a handful of self-hosted instances that are accessed via SSH (no web UI push access). Can your GitHub app work with webhooks for push events when repos are SSH-only? Do you require installing the App on every repo, or can it be org-installed?

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the details — happy to clarify before we demo. Short answers first:

- Status checks: we can operate with scoped write permissions limited to statuses/checks. The GitHub App does not need broad repo write access for that.
- SSH-only repos: webhooks are independent of git transport (SSH vs HTTPS). If the GitHub App is installed and webhooks are configured on the hosting side, we receive push events as usual. The main caveat is for self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server: we need either the org to allow apps or you to configure an app endpoint that can reach your instance (we can walk through firewall/network steps in the demo).
- Installation: org-level install is supported and preferred for most customers (saves per-repo installs). We’ll show org vs per-repo install UX in the demo.

I can take the call Wed Aug 12 at 14:30 CET — I’ll focus the session on webhook behavior, status checks, and the small network steps for on-prem/self-hosted instances. Marcus, can you send a calendar invite for 14:30–15:00 CET / 08:30–09:00 EDT?

Also attaching a quick diagram that shows where the App runs and how webhooks/keys map — should help the team follow along.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
